analyses.failure: CHK-013 — o_full_thr consistency for every 4-bit i_full_thr (61 fails / 113425 hits, first at 8648000 ps)
analyses.spec_says: REQ-FUNC-010 (rules.json:659, AF-3-14) says: "o_full_thr shall be 1 when the write-domain occupancy estimate is greater than or equal to i_full_thr ... The occupancy estimate is the binary write pointer minus the binary read pointer, where the pointer of the other domain is the synchronized one (Section 9); it is pessimistic for the full side". DEC-006 (spec md:1473, AF-20.2-05) says: "o_full_thr = occupancy >= i_full_thr ... All values are accepted". The resolved question at rules.json:12923 says "a value above the depth makes it never 1". INV-001 (rules.json:2526) says the stored count is "between 0 and PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH". Spec §9 (md:477-478) says "An invalid Gray value cannot occur in the model with one-bit changes" and the estimate "can differ from the true occupancy only by the pointer updates still inside the synchronizer". DEC-023 (md:1491) says "the destination sees only valid Gray values at any frequency". REQ-VER-001 (rules.json:2085, AF-3-71) and §10.6.4 (md:653) conflict with that: "every bit of a synchronizer is modelled independently ... a random latency, chosen independently for each bit and each change ... If the input changes again during the delay, the new value replaces the pending change and the delay restarts."
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_wr.sv:120 computes `w_occ = reg_wbin - w_rbin_s` (4-bit, modulo 16). Line 126 sets `o_full_thr = w_wr_blk ? (i_full_thr=='0) : (w_occ >= i_full_thr)`. Line 106 sets o_full from the exact Gray compare (`reg_wgray == w_rgray_s ^ 4'b1100`, which means w_occ==8), and line 125 gives `o_full = w_wr_blk | w_full_n`. Clauses (a) (thr==0) and (d) (o_full & not blocked means occ==8, so o_full_thr==(8>=thr)) cannot fail with this logic. So every failing cycle must be clause (b) (thr 9..15 with w_occ>=thr) or clause (c) (thr==8 with w_occ>=8 while o_full=0). Both need w_occ in 9..15. If w_rbin_s were a coherent past value of the read pointer, w_occ could not exceed 8: writes stop at w_occ==8 (line 109), and while blocked the flag is forced (line 126). w_rgray_s comes from u_sync_rd_gray (wr.sv:233-242), which is built from one m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync per bit. In the simulation branch, run here with +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=1 seed=1 (sim.log:27, 287-296), each bit gets its own random extra delay of 0..2 cycles. A new change replaces a pending one and restarts the delay (cell_sync.sv:149-179, output at line 182). So when the read Gray pointer changes more than once inside the 3-destination-cycle window, the synchronized vector can mix bits from different source values. Example: rd pointer 0→8 (Gray 0000→1100) with bit3 updated early and bit0 late can give 1001 = bin 14. With wbin=8 that is w_occ=10, so o_full_thr=1 while o_full=0, and clause (c) fails. This is an inference. No waveform or internal-signal dump at the fail times is in the directory.
analyses.test_does: Every test sets i_full_thr once, together with the reset (test_async_gray_fifo.py:280-288), and keeps i_rst_n_sw=1 except in the software-reset tests. Fail clusters map to tests by the sim.log timestamps. 8648–11646 ns: CHK-014 per=1 (wr 14 ns / rd 6 ns, ft=DEPTH=8, py:691-704), where the read side is faster and drains 8 words back-to-back. 140–212 µs: CHK-016 pair 1 (10/10.3). 675–798 µs: CHK-016 pair 4 (23/10). 1080–1119 µs: CHK-017 (10/14, ft=8, with software resets). 1230–1287 µs: CHK-029 pair 2 (23/10). CHK-016/029 thresholds are random 0..15 (py:761, 1373). The test-side checks of the directed thresholds compare against the formula `int(k >= ft)` (py:1518) and `int(DEPTH >= tb.ft)` (py:465), and those passed. The failing check is the SVA nnc_chk_wr.sv:123-129. Its expected values come only from the formula plus the assumption 0 <= occupancy <= DEPTH (INV-001). The failures cluster where the read pointer moves quickly relative to i_clk_wr (rd faster, or near-equal clocks with back-to-back traffic). The slow directed CHK-032 runs (5 idle edges between accesses, including ft=8 and ft=9) have no fails.

candidates.evidence_for: The incoherent synchronized pointer comes from the RTL deliverable m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-179. Each bit has an independent delay that can be restarted, so u_sync_rd_gray can output a vector the read pointer never held. That breaks the spec property "only valid Gray values" (md:477, DEC-023, EXC-001 md:1340). The flag logic then reports occupancy > DEPTH, which violates INV-001 and "a value above the depth makes it never 1" (rules.json:12923). If w_rbin_s can appear ahead of reg_wbin, the same mechanism could let the write side accept a write into an unread entry. CHK-005/006 caught none in this run, but the risk exists.
candidates.evidence_against: The model follows REQ-VER-001 / §10.6.4 to the letter (independent per bit, replace-and-restart). The flag RTL (wr.sv:120,126) implements REQ-FUNC-010 exactly. No synthesizable logic goes against a written requirement. With a coherent synchronizer (VLSIT_SYNTHESIS or the model off) w_occ<=8 by construction. CHK-005 and CHK-006 report 0 fails, so no data corruption was seen.

candidates.evidence_for: Clauses (b) and (c) of nnc_chk_wr.sv:125-127 hold only if occupancy is never above DEPTH. That assumption comes from INV-001, not from an explicit statement about o_full_thr under the metastability model.
candidates.evidence_against: The checker matches the contract text (contract.json:524) and the spec answer "a value above the depth makes it never 1" (rules.json:12923). REQ-FUNC-010 says the estimate differs from the truth only by updates inside the synchronizer, which keeps it <= DEPTH. The stimulus obeys the static-threshold rule (py:280-288, AF-3-17 decision rules.json:12788). Nothing in the test drives an illegal condition. Relaxing (b)/(c) would weaken the check and is not proposed.

candidates.evidence_for: The spec contradicts itself. REQ-VER-001 / §10.6.4 require per-bit independent random delays with replace-and-restart (rules.json:2085, md:653). §9 (md:477-478) and DEC-023 (md:1491) assume the destination only ever sees a valid, coherent Gray value and that the estimate is off only by in-flight updates. When the source pointer changes more than once within S+2 destination cycles, these cannot both hold. The fail pattern fits this mechanism: CHK-013 fails only where the read pointer (source for the write-side sync) moves fast relative to i_clk_wr, and CHK-003 (the mirror) fails only where the write pointer moves fast relative to i_clk_rd (see the next analysis). The slow, isolated-access tests (CHK-015, CHK-032) never fail. The spec does not say whether INV-001 / the threshold rules must hold with the model on.
candidates.evidence_against: No waveform confirms that w_occ was 9..15 at the fail timestamps. The mechanism is inferred from code and timing correlation. One fail (11646 ns) falls just after CHK-014 per=1 ended (11638.91 ns, during CHK-015 clock start/reset in nnc_cocotb.reset_dut, which is not in this directory), so its cause cannot be fully attributed.

analyses.options: First, confirm: re-run the same seed and dump u_vlsit_afifo_wr.w_rgray_s, w_rbin_s, w_occ, reg_wbin and the read side's reg_rgray at the NNC_FAIL timestamps. Then re-run with +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=0 (and with VLSIT_SYNTHESIS). If w_occ in 9..15 coincides with a mixed-bit w_rgray_s, and the failures disappear with the model off, the mechanism is confirmed. (1) Clarify the spec (preferred decision point). State whether the metastability model must keep a multi-bit Gray vector coherent, i.e. its output is always a value the source held, as DEC-023/§9 assume. If yes, amend REQ-VER-001/§10.6.4 (for example: the extra delay applies to the whole captured vector, or per-bit skew is limited so the output is always one of the values sampled at consecutive first-stage edges). Also state explicitly that INV-001 and the threshold rules hold with the model on. (2) Fix the RTL per that clarification. In m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-179 / m_vlsit_afifo_sync, change the model so a vector synchronizer gets one shared extra delay, or never outputs a mix of non-adjacent source values. The flag logic (wr.sv:120-126) needs no change. (3) Alternatively, if the designer decides per-bit incoherence is intended, the spec must define the allowed o_full_thr/o_full behavior when the estimate exceeds DEPTH, and whether writes may be accepted then. Separately, the possibility of overwriting unread data must be reviewed, because that would be a real functional hazard. No checker weakening is proposed.

analyses.failure: CHK-003 — o_empty_thr consistency for every 4-bit i_empty_thr (34 fails / 100200 hits, first at 231868000 ps)
analyses.spec_says: REQ-FUNC-010 (rules.json:686, AF-3-15) says: "o_empty_thr shall be 1 when the read-domain occupancy estimate is less than or equal to i_empty_thr ... pessimistic ... for the empty side (it can be smaller)". DEC-006 (md:1473) says: "o_empty_thr = occupancy <= i_empty_thr ... All values are accepted". DEC-029 / CC-11 (AF-20.2-25, AF-10.7.5-11) say that while blocked the flag takes the empty-FIFO value (o_empty_thr=1). INV-001 (rules.json:2526) bounds occupancy to 0..DEPTH, so i_empty_thr >= DEPTH should always give 1. §9 md:477-478 and DEC-023 md:1491 assume coherent Gray values. REQ-VER-001 / §10.6.4 (rules.json:2085, md:653) require per-bit independent delays with replace-and-restart. The contract text (contract.json:287) says "At every rising edge of i_clk_rd, and while i_rst_n_rd=0". That reads like a typo for =1, and the SVA checks every edge with no disable.
analyses.rtl_does: m_vlsit_afifo_rd.sv:112 computes `w_occ = w_wbin_s - reg_rbin` (4-bit modulo). Line 117 is `o_empty = w_rd_blk | w_empty_n`, with w_empty_n = (reg_rgray == w_wgray_s) (line 97). Line 118 is `o_empty_thr = w_rd_blk ? 1 : (w_occ <= i_empty_thr)`. Clause (a) cannot fail: when o_empty=1, either blocked (forced 1) or the Gray pointers are equal, so w_occ=0 <= thr. Clause (c) cannot fail: with thr=0, (w_occ==0) is equivalent to the Gray pointers being equal, which equals o_empty when not blocked. During i_rst_n_rd=0, rgray, rbin and the sync are all reset to 0, so all clauses hold. So every failing cycle must be clause (b), with i_empty_thr in 8..14 and w_occ in 9..15: the synchronized write pointer looks behind the read pointer or more than DEPTH ahead. A coherent past value of the write pointer cannot produce that, because reads stop at w_occ==0. w_wgray_s comes from u_sync_wr_gray (rd.sv:206-215), whose per-bit model cells (cell_sync.sv:149-179, enabled per sim.log:27/293-296) can output a mix of bits from different write-pointer values. That happens when the write pointer advances more than once within the S+2 read-cycle window. This is an inference. No internal dump is available.
analyses.test_does: Thresholds are set once with the reset (py:280-288). CHK-016/029 and the regression use random et in 0..15 (py:761, 1373, 1540). Fail clusters map to tests by the sim.log timestamps. 231–343 µs: CHK-016 pair 2 (wr 10 ns / rd 23 ns). 1189–1222 µs: CHK-029 pair 1 (10/23). 1374–1459 µs: test_regression_random (default 10/14, random et, software and hardware resets; both hardware resets are asserted together, py:1550-1559). In every failing run the write clock is faster than the read clock, so the write Gray pointer (the source for the read-side sync) moves fast relative to i_clk_rd. The mirror CHK-013 fails only in the opposite ratio. Directed tests with et=0 (CHK-014/017/018…) cannot hit clause (b), and the slow CHK-032 runs (et=8 and 15) never fail. The checker is nnc_chk_rd.sv:73-76. Its expected value for clause (b) comes from the assumption occupancy <= DEPTH.

candidates.evidence_for: The read-side flag reports an occupancy > DEPTH (or a negative one wrapped modulo 16). That is only possible if u_sync_wr_gray outputs a vector the write pointer never held. The cause is the per-bit independent, restartable delay in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv:149-179, which breaks the "only valid Gray values" property of md:477 / DEC-023. A synchronized write pointer that looks ahead of the true write pointer could also let the read side accept a read of an unwritten entry. CHK-005/006 saw none here, but the risk is real.
candidates.evidence_against: The model follows REQ-VER-001/§10.6.4 literally, and rd.sv:112-118 follow REQ-FUNC-010 and DEC-029 exactly. With a coherent synchronizer, w_occ is always in 0..8 and clause (b) cannot fail. CHK-005 and CHK-006 report 0 fails.

candidates.evidence_for: The contract behavior text (contract.json:287) says "while i_rst_n_rd=0", but nnc_chk_rd.sv:73 checks at every edge with no disable iff. The check description and the SVA do not match. Clause (b) relies on INV-001 rather than on an explicit statement for the model-on case.
candidates.evidence_against: The mismatch does not cause these failures: during reset the RTL output satisfies all clauses (rd.sv:117-118 with reset pointers and sync), and the failures occur in mid-traffic runs. Clause (b) matches DEC-006 + INV-001 and the resolved spec answer (rules.json:12923, mirrored for the empty side). Stimulus respects the static-threshold rule. Relaxing (b) would weaken the check and is not proposed.

candidates.evidence_for: Same conflict as for CHK-013. REQ-VER-001/§10.6.4 (per-bit independent delay, replace-and-restart) conflicts with §9 md:477-478 and DEC-023 (coherent Gray value, estimate off only by in-flight updates) whenever the source pointer changes more than once within S+2 destination cycles. The direction-dependence fits that mechanism exactly: CHK-003 fails only with fast write / slow read (10/23, 10/14), and CHK-013 only with fast read (14/6, 23/10, ~10/10). The spec does not state whether INV-001 and the threshold rules must hold with the model enabled. The contract's "while i_rst_n_rd=0" wording is also ambiguous.
candidates.evidence_against: No waveform proves w_occ in 9..15 at the fail times. The conclusion rests on code reading plus timestamp-to-test and clock-ratio correlation. The random et values for each run are not logged, so clause (b) is inferred as the failing clause, not observed.

analyses.options: First, confirm: re-run seed 1 and dump u_vlsit_afifo_rd.w_wgray_s, w_wbin_s, reg_rbin, w_occ, i_empty_thr and the write side's reg_wgray at the CHK-003 fail timestamps. Also log the random et per test. Then re-run with +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN=0 and with VLSIT_SYNTHESIS to see whether the failures disappear. (1) Clarify the spec: decide whether the metastability model must preserve multi-bit Gray coherence (as DEC-023/§9 assume), and state that INV-001 and the threshold rules hold with the model on. Fix the contract wording of CHK-003 from "while i_rst_n_rd=0" to the intended condition. The SVA already checks every edge, including reset, and the RTL meets it there. (2) If coherence is required, fix the RTL model in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.sv / m_vlsit_afifo_sync: one shared extra delay per synchronized vector, or a constraint so the output is always a value sampled at a first-stage edge. No change is needed in rd.sv flag logic. (3) If per-bit incoherence is intended, the spec must define o_empty_thr/o_empty behavior when the read-domain estimate is outside 0..DEPTH, and whether reads may then be accepted, because this could be a data-integrity hazard. No checker weakening is proposed.
